headline: BNP Acting Chairman Tarek Rahman is visiting the US
summary: The senior BNP leader is traveling to the United States for a series of meetings and diplomatic engagements.
details: BNP Acting Chairman Tarek Rahman is traveling to the United States. This visit comes at a critical time for Bangladesh's political landscape.
While the specific agenda of the visit has not been detailed, it is expected that he will meet with various diplomatic officials and political leaders.
The visit is seen as an effort to engage with international partners and discuss the current political situation in Bangladesh.
Tarek Rahman has been residing in London for several years, and this move to the US is part of his ongoing diplomatic outreach.

headline: 839 hospitalised in 24 hours as 5 more die of dengue
summary: Daily hospitalisations hit a yearly high as total dengue deaths in Bangladesh rise to 82, with nearly 29,000 cases recorded so far this year.
details: At least five dengue patients died and 839 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours ending yesterday morning. This marks the highest single-day hospitalisation count recorded so far this year.

Of the deceased, three were from Dhaka South City Corporation, while one each was from the Dhaka and Khulna divisions. The total number of dengue deaths has now risen to 82, with total cases reaching 28,929.
Currently, 1,951 dengue patients are receiving treatment in hospitals across the country. Experts suggest that cases may continue to rise through October before declining in November.
Prof Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University emphasized the need to identify neighbourhood-level hotspots and intensify mosquito control and community awareness campaigns.
Medical experts advise patients to seek evaluations at the onset of fever, on the third or fourth day, and again after the fever subsides.
Immediate medical attention is urged if warning signs appear, such as severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, breathing difficulties, or bleeding.
caption:
839 people hospitalised in a single day—the highest count this year. 5 more have died from dengue.

At least five dengue patients died and 839 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours ending yesterday morning. This marks the highest single-day hospitalisation count recorded so far this year.

Of the deceased, three were from Dhaka South City Corporation, while one each was from the Dhaka and Khulna divisions. The total number of dengue deaths has now risen to 82, with total cases reaching 28,929.

Currently, 1,951 dengue patients are receiving treatment in hospitals across the country. Experts suggest that cases may continue to rise through October before declining in November.

Prof Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University emphasized the need to identify neighbourhood-level hotspots and intensify mosquito control and community awareness campaigns.

Medical experts advise patients to seek evaluations at the onset of fever, on the third or fourth day, and again after the fever subsides.

Immediate medical attention is urged if warning signs appear, such as severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, breathing difficulties, or bleeding.
